verdict.rationale: Lithic's Auth Rules engine lets users define rules on attributes like MCC, country, currency and risk score. These rules are evaluated automatically across several event streams: card authorizations, 3DS, tokenization and ACH receipts. Shadow mode and backtesting help validate draft rules. However, the documented actions are limited to authorization decisioning, not general event-triggered actions. Webhooks and ASA only deliver events to user-built endpoints, so any broader action logic is the user's own code. missing for 10: documented rule actions beyond approve/decline decisioning (e.g., notify, freeze card, call webhook on rule match), a general event-to-action automation builder, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: By defining rules based on high-signal attributes like MCC, country, currency, and risk score, you can enforce business-specific authorization logic at the program, account, or card level, without managing additional infrastructure.

the Auth Rules engine supports multiple event streams, each enabling decisioning for a different payment flow: card authorizations, 3DS authentication, digital wallet and merchant tokenization, and ACH receipts.
shadow mode lets draft rules observe the authorization stream without affecting outcomes, while performance reports and backtesting measure impact over time
